instructions: Pat the squid tubes very dry with paper towels, inside and out. Cut them into 1/2 inch rings.
Put the 3/4 cup flour and 3/4 tsp of the salt in a large zip bag and shake it to mix.
Split the 4 demi-baguettes lengthwise, leaving them joined along one side. Chop 1/4 cup of the parsley. Cut the lemon into wedges. Line a plate with paper towels.
Heat a large frying pan over medium high heat and add the 3/4 cup oil. Give it about 3 minutes. It's ready when a squid ring dropped in sizzles right away.
Add a third of the rings to the bag and shake until they're evenly coated. Shake off the extra flour in your hands.
Add them to the pan in a single layer with a little room between them. Stand back a little. They'll spatter. Fry until the underside is golden, about 1 1/2 minutes.
Turn them and cook the other side for about 1 1/2 minutes, until golden and crisp. Transfer them to the paper towels and sprinkle them with a pinch of the salt.
Coat and fry the rest of the rings the same way in two batches, salting each batch as it comes out.
Fill each baguette with the hot squid and scatter the parsley over it. Serve with the lemon wedges.
method_notes: All three coat squid rings in seasoned flour, fry them until golden and crisp, salt them as they come out and pile them hot into a split baguette. Spain on a Fork (the lead) shallow fries the rings in sunflower oil in a frying pan and finishes with parsley; Jose Pizarro (Broadsheet) deep fries them with pimentón in the flour and spreads the bread with aioli, and The Takeout adds shrimp, butters and toasts the rolls and uses a lemon aioli. None had 20 ratings and RecipeTin Eats has no version, so this follows Spain on a Fork, scaled to four sandwiches, with lemon wedges on the side as the Madrid bars serve it and no aioli.
